27 minutes with Ariane 5. 8 years to reach Mercury. 🚀

On 20 October 2018, BepiColombo lifted off from Europe’s Spaceport aboard Ariane 5.

Around 27 minutes later, the spacecraft separated from the launcher and began the next stage of its journey: an eight-year voyage through the inner Solar System to reach Mercury.

A few minutes with Ariane 5 were the first step in a journey lasting billions of kilometres.

From launch to separation, every minute was about putting BepiColombo on the right path for what came next.

#LaunchingAmbitions
@esa @JAXA_jp @CNES

What can worlds millions of kilometres away teach us about our own? 🔭

From Mercury to Jupiter and its icy moons, scientific missions help us better understand how planets form, evolve and interact with their environments.

Eight years ago today, BepiColombo began its journey to Mercury. 🚀

On 20 October 2018, the ESA/JAXA mission lifted off from Europe’s Spaceport aboard Ariane 5, beginning one of the most complex journeys through the inner Solar System.

Since then, BepiColombo has travelled billions of kilometres, using planetary flybys to gradually adjust its trajectory towards the closest planet to the Sun.

Eight years after launch, the journey that began in Kourou is entering its final chapter, bringing BepiColombo closer to the world it was built to explore.

A journey that started with Ariane 5, and continues to push our understanding of Mercury further.

#LaunchingAmbitions
@esa @JAXA_jp @CNES

📣 Announcement: ispace has been selected by JAXA as a contractor for its competitive proposal solicitation, “Conceptual Design for the Realization of a Lunar Solar Power Tower (Parts A-B)"

As lunar activities continue to expand, a stable power supply will be a critical component of the infrastructure needed to enable sustained operations on the lunar surface, with a projected requirement on the order of tens of kilowatts (kW) by the early 2030s. 

ispace will proceed with arrangements to finalize a contract with JAXA and will work with partner companies on the conceptual design of the lunar solar power tower and its power distribution system for lunar surface equipment. Drawing on the expertise and experience gained through its lunar exploration missions and lander development programs, ispace will contribute to defining system requirements and specifications, interfaces with lunar landers, and plans for future development.

“As activities on the lunar surface gain momentum, developing essential infrastructure—including power, communications, and positioning capabilities—will become increasingly important alongside transportation. We are very pleased to have the opportunity to participate in JAXA’s conceptual design initiative for a lunar solar power tower," said Takeshi Hakamada, Founder & CEO, ispace, inc.

Read more here:

@JAXA_jp @JAXA_en

We're thrilled to announce we have signed an MoU with ALTEC, an Italian centre of excellence for engineering and logistics services supporting space operations and planetary exploration missions.

Testing, simulation, and operator training in analogue lunar environments are essential to successful lunar surface operations. Under the MoU, we will assess opportunities for ispace-EUROPE to use ALTEC facilities to simulate rover platform operations in lunar analogue environments.

Through this collaboration, we have the opportunity to bring together ispace-EUROPE’s expertise in lunar rover development and operations with ALTEC’s advanced facilities and expertise testing for planetary mission operations.

With ALTEC owned by Thales Alenia Space and the Italian Space Agency (ASI), this agreement reflects the growing strength of Europe’s lunar exploration ecosystem. 

By working with leading partners across Europe we can accelerate the development of robust, operationally ready rover systems that support future science, exploration and space resource utilization missions on the Moon 🇮🇹🇱🇺🌙

Read more 🔗
